Author: @Locust13
Content: Regarding the topic of near-death experiences, no one has actually died and come back. That's why it's called NEAR death experience. And there's perfectly natural neuroscience explanations for these experiences. One of the things an oxygen deprived brain does to protect itself regarding myelonic sheaths is release literal DMT. A known hallucinogenic chemical floods the brain and pools into the back of it. The idea that an oxygen-deprived, damaged, malfunctioning brain that is flooded with a hallucinogenic drug is relaying an actual experience instead of a hallucination is genuinely too stupid to consider.
